description:
Lindor by Lindt are a WORK OF ART, let's make some ice cream using the Lindor Balls. 

What you will need:

Milk (2%) 586g
Cream (heavy or double) 400g
Cocoa powder (Guittards ideally as its a perfect one to go with the Lindor) 40g
135g Lindor balls (12 balls) 
Sugar 100g
Dextrose 151g
Skimmed Milk Poweder 55g
Stabilizer 1.3g (Optional)

If you can't get Lindor balls where you are, not only are you missing out on one of the GREATEST sweets in the world, this recipe will not really be much use to you. 

If you CAN get them, I recommend you get on this right away!! CHOP CHOP

Hi, I am from Switzerland and this chocolat, Lindor is everywhere. I just wanted to say, in Lindor the taste is pretty low, it's a very sugary chocolat, I would definitely not recommend it for ice cream. The are two giant chocolat companies here Lindor and Cailler, Cailler produce a chocolat called Frigor. Frigor is by far the best chocolat for an ice cream, the taste is much richer and it's less sugary. Really a perfect match, because most chocolat taste bitter/numb when cold, and this one doesn't. It taste very similar to the chocolat found on the tip of a Winnetou popsicle. If you have an opportunity to put you hands on some I really recommend.

PS: If you use any Cailler chocolat, Cailler also make high end cocoa powder...
PS: Lindt also make Lindt cocoa powder...

comments.text: Looks great Nick. What is your opinion of adding cream last instead of the beginning when everything is heating up. Thanks
comments.author: @GreenMonkiCoffee2008

comments.text:
I don’t often make cold process ice cream but will do a video about it soon. 
Heating the milk only allows the denaturing of the whey protein which helps to stabilize the air in the resulting mix. Doing the same to the cream has essentially no benefit when making at home and very little benefit when making in commercial machines as we generally use stabilizers in that environment. If you are using a stabilizer in your mix, heating the entire mix is a waste of time. Adding the cream after helps to rapidly cool the milk mix much faster and is my usual method. 
I do like to try new methods though and make notes on the results.
